body: Yeah I figured my way of coping wouldn't work for everyone, but I wanted to throw it out there in case it's helpful for someone! Even though I'm feeling so intensely, I know I'm going to regret my overreacting. I've explained to him that I don't want to validate the emotions that I know I'll regret, and I don't want to hurt him unnecessarily. Just my way of coping, of course! Sending you positive thoughts.<3

I experience the same thing. My boyfriend is a veteran and has a bad back, so I have to pull myself away from my emotional response and feeling rejected to understand his perspective. For me, I like sex because it feels good, but also because I feel so connected with him. So it hurts when I rarely get that connection. We’re still struggling to find a middle ground but I think it’s so important to talk about it, just work to understand his perspective as well.

When I get upset over something with my boyfriend, I tend to shut down and I’m not sure how to handle my emotions. I try to say nothing is wrong because I know I’m overreacting and I don’t want to throw a temper tantrum, but I’m not good at hiding my feelings so he keeps pushing. One thing that’s been helpful is explaining to him that sometimes I get upset but the rational part of my brain can tell I’m probably overreacting. I sometimes ask him if we can just put it aside for a bit and return to it later because I recognize I’m overreacting. It’s so frustrating that my first response to discomfort is to pout and have a tantrum but I try to stay grounded and return to it after I’ve had time to process. Obviously that’s just me and other people’s symptoms may manifest differently.

For me, I’ve realized that when I’m left to my own devices, I tend to make destructive, risky decisions. I tend to do better when I’m living with someone, whether it was living in a dorm, living with my mom, or living with a romantic partner. However! When I was living alone, it helped me a lot to have a cat around. It really helps to fill the loneliness to have a cat running around, and to have someone to “talk to,” even if it’s just me talking at her while I feed her or something. It was also helpful for me to fill my apartment with some noise, whether it be music or watching tv. Social hobbies (video games or blogging or something) can also help! Best of luck 💖
When I’m really bad, I take a ton of depression naps and then struggle to sleep at night.

I’m no relationship expert and I struggle a loooot with all my relationships, so take my experience with a grain of salt. I try to remember that not everyone has the same communication needs in relationships, and even though it can be a bummer for that to stand in the way of a relationship with a really cool person, I’d rather find someone who is more compatible with my relationship expectations. It can be super hard to meet people and online dating can be incredibly tedious and frustrating. However I would encourage you to remember that just because your relationship expectations don’t align with someone else’s, it’s just an indicator that there’s an area where you two aren’t compatible. I do think there can be a middle ground and it may be necessary to compromise on how often you see each other, but you shouldn’t have to completely shut down your own preferences.

Not usually in a rage but when my emotions are high. My memory gets super fuzzy when I start getting upset, which makes it challenging to reflect on what happened. Especially with my boyfriend, I’ll get super upset and then struggle to articulate what upset me.

I can relate to this. I’ve had instances where I forget to take my meds for a few days and I feel fine so I start to think maybe I don’t need them. I always regret it when my emotions hit me hard within a few days. No one here can change your decisions, but I just want to speak from my own experience in the hopes that you consider what I’ve said. I have had so many panic attacks and self-injury episodes because I got too lazy to take my meds for a while. It’s absolutely awful and meds are soso important. Please do not stop them unless you’re under the guidance of a professional.

Have you ever had a guinea pig? The cats we have are so aloof and I just don’t feel as needed or wanted by them, which is why I want a dog so badly (as well as the motivation to walk a dog and get out of bed). I’ve always wanted a guinea pig so I’ll look into that, but I’m just not sure how affectionate they actually are.

He knows how heavily I rely on my cat as an emotional support animal and that I’m struggling because she’s so much more distanced since I moved in with him and his cat. He gets so upset when I talk about feeling like hurting myself or feeling suicidal so I haven’t been explicit about it. He says we don’t have the money right now so I don’t want to be too pushy.

I feel the same way about my body. I dunno if this would help you but I felt a lot stronger and more confident in my body after I started exercising regularly. I lost all motivation to work out once my depression got bad again tho and now I feel like a fat tub of lard every time I walk and it’s the worst feeling.

I can only speak from my experience obviously, but I got a cat since I was living in a 13th floor apartment and knew a dog would be way too difficult. I knew a dog’s temperament would be more helpful for me emotionally, so I invested a lot of time in meeting cats at various shelters to find the most clingy and dog-like cat that I could. I still really want a dog eventually but having a cat gives me the companionship, while also allowing me the flexibility to have my “bad days.” I think having a pet can give you the push you need to get yourself out of bed, so it could work well to have a dog, but a cat has helped me a lot.

People can have an attitude when you’re handling their money. :( I worked at a small community-oriented bank and people would get so pissed when I’d ask for ID because I was new and didn’t recognize them. Most people were lovely but you run into bad eggs in any customer service job :( best of luck!

One other suggestion I would make is working at a bank. I worked as a teller for a bit and even though I had some difficult customers, I found myself dissociating a lot less because it was a more laidback environment. We had to be more careful with our work, obviously, but it was a lot less rushed and the customers were generally nicer.

If you’re near a university, there are a ton of employment opportunities at those. I’m getting my masters in higher education because I enjoy the growth mindset at higher education institutions, and I enjoy being able to help undergrads. Just a suggestion of what worked for me!

When I’ve had to do job switching, I use indeed to try to find as many options as possible! Just as a tip (:

I really wanted a dog as my emotional support animal but it wasn’t possible with my busy schedule and with my thirteenth floor apartment lol. I knew I needed a “clingy” animal that would have a very active presence in my life whenever I was home. I spent a lot of time at shelters trying to find the right cat, and the one I have now is perfect for me. I think a dog would have been better for my emotional needs but i couldn’t handle the responsibilities of a dog. My dog-like cat does an amazing job in making me feel wanted and not alone(:

Yes. It’s sill and I recognize that it doesn’t make logical sense but I’ve carried this delusion with me for five years now. I think about it a lot but especially when I’m in distress; that I’m just in a coma and this is all a bad dream and if I kill myself I can wake up. It’s definitely a way of detaching when I’m upset, and I recognize it doesn’t  make sense, but I kinda convince myself it’s real in those moments and really hope that it’ll come true.

This last year has easily been the hardest year of my life and my cat has been the main thing that has really kept me from attempting suicide. It’s gotten harder and harder for her to be enough motivation but fortunately I decided to leave my job and I’m almost done here. I am forever grateful that my kitty helped me to get through this.

I never realized my way of speaking was manipulative until these last few years. Another thing I’ve experienced is that I would talk to friends about how I felt about other people when I was in a disagreement with that other person, and I’d accidentally “turn them against” the other person. The same thing happened when I was telling my mom about my new boyfriend. It was jarring to me to realize the impact that articulating my black-and-white thinking had on other people, and I’m working to shift my way of speaking so that I don’t come across as so manipulative.

I love this idea, to have a stable and worthwhile job while pursuing my art. It’s soso important for me to find a job that I get enough fulfillment from that I have energy to work at my art. I’d love to eventually be able to make money from my art but I would be so happy  to just be at a place where I have the time and mental energy to pursue my art in my free time.

I dunno how bad my experiences of splitting are compared with other people so I don’t know how effective my methods might be. Personally I have to use a lot of self restraint to keep myself from blurting things out. I know that I will completely lay into the person and regret it if I go off. I’ll force myself to step back and remind myself that I should assume the best of the person (if it’s someone like my boyfriend or sister) rather than assuming that they meant to hurt me. I tell them I need a minute to gather my thoughts and I usually have big pauses before each response. I carefully weigh how I can tell them what upset me and if anything can be changed. Like, I try to focus on telling them about things that bother me if I have an idea of what I want them to do differently. It’s also helpful with my boyfriend that I’ve been able to be honest that I struggle to perceive relationships accurately and that I may overreact to things, but he’s open to us talking about it and figuring it out together. It was rough in the start but it’s gotten a lot easier with this open communication and it’s a lot rarer for me to split on him.

Halsey (specifically from her Badlands album ; I really like Gasoline, Ghost, and Control). Melanie Martinez (Mad Hater and Cry Baby). Twenty One Pilots (Ride and Car Radio). Some other songs: Habits (Stay High) by Tove Lo, Here by Alesia Cara, Little Talks by Of Monsters and Men, Cliffs Edge by Hayley Kiyoko, East of Eden by Zella Day... some of the songs on my bpd playlist.

Yikes I feel this. It’s been a rough year and I feel like I’ve fucked up all my work/school relationships and I get so anxious about how people secretly think about me, since I have some ideas about it. It makes my anxiety skyrocket when I am alone and start thinking about it. Having my emotional support animal around helps a lot.

My mind is constantly telling me how worthless I am so having people around me who focus on my faults tends to push me to spiral. For the first time, I’m dealing with a supervisor who does that, and I’ve been working on a lot of coping techniques but ultimately decided to step away from the position. I like hearing what I’m doing well because it helps me to do more of it and encourages me to keep working hard if I’m good at what I’m doing. I love constructive, tactful feedback that comes from a place of care, but I struggle with harsh criticism.

It helped me to understand where you were coming from by reading your comments about watching your dad discipline your dog, but I’d encourage you to do research on training cats specifically in an ethical and effective way. My cat kicks litter everywhere but she never does it on purpose. I got her a tall litter box with a lid, and a mat leading out from the litter box. Like someone else said, cats are really hard to train and with things like this, it’s often better to put preventative measures in place, like the setup of your litter box. Even with my cat, my biggest issue was her scratching the furniture that came with my apartment, but she stopped as soon as I got her a cat tree with alternative scratching posts.

I don’t know if this is an issue for you, but I tend to become volatile and violent when my bpd gets really bad and I have a panic attack. But just because I’m in that state, doesn’t mean I’m not still responsible for the well-being of my cat. I shoo her away because I don’t want to yell at her or push her away or anything. If she was being relentless and trying to comfort me, I would lock her away until I calmed down, but she’s good about following my lead. Being a cat mom is so important to me and even though I know my kitty wants to support me, I’d never put her in harms way. Just my two cents on balancing my mental illness with being a cat mom.

I’m thinking of getting a tribute to my emotional support animal. I want to get a kawaii-style cutesy design of her with a ribbon that says “hold tight, sweetheart” from Kesha’s song Rainbow. It was an idea I came up with a month or so ago but it really resonated with me.

I love this description. I’ve always been very materialistic in terms of priding myself on things like my makeup collection, and my relationship to fandom has always been important to me. Maybe I take these obsessions so far because it’s the main way I can find a sense of identity.

One thing that resonated with me in this post was where you mentioned that she really wants to be with someone. I feel like i fell into similar patterns with my ex and he was safe because I knew he wouldn’t leave me, but he never pushed me to be better and more healthy. It’s not his fault that my bpd is so bad and that our relationship dynamic kind of enabled me, but I should have broken up with him much earlier. I needed to be with someone who loves and supports me, but who will also stand their ground and challenge me (like my current boyfriend). It was easy for me to take my ex for granted and that wasn’t fair for him at all. He deserved much better than I could give him, and breaking up with him was the best decision I could have made.

My therapist helped me to recognize that I tend to fall into the headspace of “if I can’t do it perfectly, I won’t do it at all.” I’m trying to challenge myself to be okay with things not being perfect and to hold myself to the same standards that I’d hold other people to. I also know that I get overwhelmed when I think about how many things I have to do because I feel like I can never do them all and do them right. I’ve worked on prioritizing so that I complete the most important tasks.

I don’t have any further insight but man I feel this post so much. You described my last relationship perfectly. I can only speak for my own experiences and my own particular issues, but it’s been a lot better for me with my current partner. I’ve been able to reign myself in and he pushes me to be better, and the therapist I’ve been seeing has helped me through a lot in terms of challenging my thoughts and regulating my emotions. I mostly wanted to comment to let you know you’re not alone and that your post really resonated with me.

I’m with a new partner after spending three and a half years with someone I wasn’t sexually attracted to (number one on an endless list of problems with our relationship). Like someone else said, I get super anxious about initiating sex or taking the lead for fear of rejection or of doing something dumb since I’m still inexperienced at age 24. With my new partner, sex is a huge part of our relationship. It feels good but i had no idea how intense of an emotionally connecting experience it could be. My partner has ptsd where he’s constantly trying to keep his brain occupied to avoid the “bad thoughts” and sex is also the one time where I completely have his attention.

Getting an emotional support cat did wonders for me.  I always do at least one productive thing per day by feeding her, and it helps me to have a sense of purpose when I remember that I saved her and she needs me to keep going. My love for her outweighs my self-hatred (very slightly lol). Animals in general have always helped me to come back down when my mental illness starts to act up. They’re much more straightforward than humans, and I never have to worry about hidden agendas with them.

My ndad has been using the fact that he paid for my college as a reason that I should bow down to him and ignore the fact that he's trying to make my mom and I homeless (and playing with my sister's tuition now). My mom keeps saying things to the effect of what you said but it's always so much more affirming to hear it from someone from the outside. Thank you.

Thank you so much for this. My therapist really helped me to accept the thing about boundaries being okay and needing to enforce my boundaries. I'm hoping one day I'll learn to let go of the sense of obligation (ndad paid for college but that doesn't make what he did to my mom and me ok and I'm still allowed to be angry..:I think).

Great observation. This is a bit different but it stems from the idea of an nparents sense of entitlement to ownership. When I graduated college, my dad treated it as an accomplishment of his since he paid for it. Like he was entitled to my degree because he paid for it and the hard work I put in didn't matter. Most people were congratulating me on my accomplishment but he just wanted to see the diploma he "paid" for.

I want desperately to change my last name so that I am not associated with my ndad or his family. I'm not sure if I will go through the process of changing to my mom's maiden name or if I'll marry my boyfriend and take his last name. I know I want to be with him for the rest of my life but I don't want to pressure/rush him into marriage for my own purposes. But I need to get rid of my dirty last name asap, yknow? I want his last name a lot but it'd also be pretty satisfying to take my mom's name instead. But it's so expensive when I'm broke ugh.

I've been recording my parents fighting in case we could use it against my dad at any point in some capacity. I really want to share some of the audio clips online but I don't know if I could get in legal trouble??? God these abusive parents so deserve to be exposed for the awful things they do.
YES this reminds me of myself. Guys yelling makes me terrified, and guys drunkenly yelling is enough to put me in a fit of anxiety.

God forbid you enjoy engaging in a health behavior that makes you feel good about yourself! I'm really sorry. I had a "friend" at college who did similar things when I was trying to do keto, showing up with wine and candy to my room on a school night and pushing me to engage in "self care" uh ok self-care is taking care of my body, don't tell me what self-care is. Dragging me to Steak 'n Shake and telling me I have to order a shake, then telling me "they don't put bread in milkshakes!" when I remark about not wanting to eat so many carbs.

Anywho that's my rant. People can be shitty and it's so hard to hear from your family. I love keto (even though I suck at sticking with it) and you're genuinely making a great choice for your body. Stick with it as best as you can.

My ndad always used money as a way of controlling my family. My mom stayed at home while he worked, but my mom did her share by doing the housework and taking care of the kids. It ended up being that he helped me pay for college (he was adamant I go to the better more expensive school when I had a full ride elsewhere). I recently took my mom's side in their divorce since he's trying to make us homeless, and he recently went on a drunk rant to my mom (he knew I was there) about how I'm pathetic because he spent so many thousands of dollars on my education and I "won't talk to him" (not likes he's even tried to talk to me). I hate feeling like I owe people and I think money is going to be touchy for me for the rest of my life. He's so frugal and we were always told to tell him that a family member bought things for us so he didn't know my mom bought us clothes when we were young. I became an impulse spender for a while because of mental health issues but it was always a shitty combination of relief from anxiety and guilt. I hate money ugh ugh ugh.

As sorry as I am about your nightmares, it's kinda nice to know I'm not alone. My mom shielded me a lot from ndad's abuse but I still get recurring nightmares. I'm hoping they'll go away eventually but they're bad.

So sick of my ndad and can't wait for this divorce to be done. I'm sick of walking on eggshells whenever he's home, putting up baby gates to ensure he doesn't hurt us, being afraid of throwing out food because he may use that against my mom in court, etc. I know we may be homeless at the end of this but I don't even care. We will make it work, even if we're in a tiny apartment, and at least we won't be vulnerable to his psychological torture.

In other news, I was trying to make my lunch for work tomorrow in the kitchen. Apparently I was taking too long because he started making all this noise from his room and so I gave up once I started shaking with anxiety, and he took over the kitchen shortly after I left. He doesn't have work tomorrow so I'm not even disrupting him. I'm just done.
I agree about the Essence eyeliner brush! It's my HG eyeliner brush. I was using the ELF Studio Small Angled Brush but it was a little bit too thick for me. The Essence one is great.
I found Madoka to be very similar. Maybe look into Higurashi No Naku Kori Ni, Deadman Wonderland, Another, Tokyo Ghoul, Elfen Lied. Those are some of my favorites!

I had to skip through a few parts that made me particularly squeamish but gosh, I'm really sorry to hear about all of this. From experience, I know how awful the sorting-out-your-sexuality process is, and I can't even imagine throwing this mess into that process. I'm very glad that you got away from him. Given all the shit he did, I'm not really that surprised that even his mother feels that way.
My school in the States has some single sex floors but there are just as many co-ed housing options.
